science.title: Multifunctional spacecraft radiation shield based on an HBGPE composite with modelled scintillation-based energy conversion and boron-10 neutron capture
science.description: Deep-space missions require substantial shielding mass, yet conventional shields dissipate absorbed particle energy as wasted heat. Here we present RADIANT, a six-layer composite combining a hydrogen-boron-graphene polyethylene (HBGPE) layer, a cerium oxide-loaded scintillation layer, and a graphene-polycaprolactone layer intended for charge collection. Geant4 11.2.2 simulations across 35 configurations show 2.14-fold higher neutron attenuation than equivalent-thickness aluminium at 1 MeV, driven by hydrogen moderation rather than boron-10 capture at fast-neutron energies; at equal areal density this rises to 2.53-fold. Boron-10 was modelled at both 95% enrichment (an optimisation scenario) and the natural abundance (~ 19.9% ¹⁰B) of the prototype, giving 19.02% attenuation. Infrared testing showed stable electrical output spanning 0.69 to 131.05 W·m⁻² under controlled thermal input, with the transduction mechanism uncharacterised. A model-based calculation combining Geant4 energy deposition with literature-derived scintillator parameters projects particle-driven conversion efficiencies of 0.00–0.0107%, pending ionising-radiation validation. In bench tests, the outer tungsten surface reached a pyrometer-estimated 545 °C with output retention above 93%, and the prototype withstood 100 N of compressive load with partial structural compromise, no fracture, at 14.9% lower areal density than equal-thickness aluminium. These results establish simulated neutron-shielding gains and an unconfirmed pathway toward radiation-to-electrical conversion in shielding mass.

science.title: Microglia mediate motor memory decay through activity-dependent phagocytosis of myelin sheaths
science.description: Experience-dependent changes in myelination are important for motor learning, with newly generated oligodendrocytes contributing to the formation of new myelin. However, motor memories decay over time and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unexplored. Here we show that motor memory decay is linked to changes in memory-associated myelin sheaths resulting from microglial phagocytosis in mouse brain. Mechanistically, reduced activity of motor memory engram cells lowers oligodendrocyte expression of the ‘don’t eat me’ signal from Cluster of differentiation 47 (CD47), facilitating microglial phagocytosis and driving myelin loss. Knockout of CD47 from motor memory-associated oligodendrocytes increased microglial phagocytosis of myelin sheaths and accelerated the decay of motor memory, whereas overexpression of CD47 showed opposite results. Moreover, microglia phagocytose myelin sheaths and synapses independently. Our findings reveal that microglial phagocytosis of motor memory-associated myelin sheaths leads to the decay of motor memory. Since various types of memory require myelination in the brain, this mechanism may contribute to the decay of other memory types. Hu et al. showed that motor memory decay involves microglia engulfing memory-related myelin sheaths. Reduced engram activity lowers CD47, a ‘don’t eat me’ signal, thus promoting microglia-mediated myelin clearance and facilitating memory decay.

science.title: Entanglement-based quantum key distribution with classical signals in hollow-core fiber
science.description: The coexistence of quantum information and classical signals in a single fiber is essential for future quantum networks that leverage the well-established optical fiber infrastructure. Although multiplexing technologies can separate quantum and classical signals, pure silica core fibers (PSCFs) remain fundamentally limited by the high nonlinearity, which generates substantial Raman scattering and four-wave mixing noise. Hollow-core fibers (HCFs), guiding light predominantly in air, offer an attractive solution with intrinsically ultra-low nonlinearity and strongly suppressed nonlinear noise. In this work, we demonstrate the entanglement-based key coexisting with data over an 18-km HCF link. We achieve time-encoded high-dimensional quantum key distribution (HD-QKD) carrying 0 dBm of bidirectional received power, corresponding to a theoretical data capacity of up to 2.3 Tbps. During 24 h of continuous operation, an average secret key rate (SKR) of 10.56 kbps is obtained. Theoretical analysis further predicts SKRs above 135 kbps over transmission distances exceeding 200 km using state-of-the-art low-loss HCFs. These results show significantly improved performance compared with PSCF-based systems and highlight the potential of HCFs for scalable quantum-classical coexistence compatible with the architectures of established fiber-optic networks

science.title: Dragon fruit peel waste-derived iron nanozyme with peroxidase-like activity for smartphone-assisted colorimetric detection of urinary uric acid
science.description: Uric acid monitoring is important for the early identification and management of hyperuricemia, which is linked to gout and an increased risk of metabolic and cardiovascular disorders. Turning agricultural and food-processing waste into useful functional materials also offers a more sustainable path for developing low-cost analytical tools. Here, we developed a simple colorimetric method for detecting uric acid using a nanozyme made from dragon fruit peel, an abundant agricultural waste material. This nanozyme mimics the activity of natural peroxidase enzymes, converting a colorless substrate into a blue-colored product in the presence of hydrogen peroxide. Uric acid was found to inhibit this colorimetric reaction, with the intensity of the blue color decreasing as uric acid concentration increased. The colorimetric assay exhibited a linear response over a uric acid concentration range of 0–100 µM, with a limit of detection (LOD) of 3.49 µM. The method was applied to uric acid detection in rat urine samples using a smartphone camera for colorimetric readout. High concentration of calcium and magnesium ions were found to cause some interference with uric acid detection. These findings support the use of dragon fruit peel-derived nanozymes as a practical platform for affordable, point-of-care uric acid monitoring.
